title: Real Estate Sales Agents
description: Rent, buy, or sell property for clients. Perform duties such as study property listings, interview prospective clients, accompany clients to property site, discuss conditions of sale, and draw up real estate contracts. Includes agents who represent buyer.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Answer clients' questions regarding construction work, financing, maintenance, repairs, and appraisals.
Advise sellers on how to make homes more appealing to potential buyers.
Advise clients on market conditions, prices, mortgages, legal requirements, and related matters.
Accompany buyers during visits to and inspections of property, advising them on the suitability and value of the homes they are visiting.
Evaluate mortgage options to help clients obtain financing at the best prevailing rates and terms.
Generate lists of properties that are compatible with buyers' needs and financial resources.
Interview clients to determine what kinds of properties they are seeking.
Arrange for title searches to determine whether clients have clear property titles.
Solicit and compile listings of available rental properties.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Compare a property with similar properties that have recently sold to determine its competitive market price.
Appraise properties to determine loan values.
Visit properties to assess them before showing them to clients.
Coordinate property closings, overseeing signing of documents and disbursement of funds.
Contact utility companies for service hookups to clients' property.
Secure construction or purchase financing with own firm or mortgage company.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Present purchase offers to sellers for consideration.
Act as an intermediary in negotiations between buyers and sellers, generally representing one or the other.
Prepare documents such as representation contracts, purchase agreements, closing statements, deeds, and leases.
Review plans for new construction with clients, enumerating and recommending available options and features.
Coordinate appointments to show homes to prospective buyers.
Arrange meetings between buyers and sellers when details of transactions need to be negotiated.
Confer with escrow companies, lenders, home inspectors, and pest control operators to ensure that terms and conditions of purchase agreements are met before closing dates.
Promote sales of properties through advertisements, open houses, and participation in multiple listing services.
Contact previous clients for prospecting of referral business.
Review property listings, trade journals, and relevant literature, and attend conventions, seminars, and staff and association meetings, to remain knowledgeable about real estate markets.
Contact property owners and advertise services to solicit property sales listings.
Display commercial, industrial, agricultural, and residential properties to clients and explain their features.
Develop networks of attorneys, mortgage lenders, and contractors to whom clients may be referred.
Investigate clients' financial and credit status to determine eligibility for financing.
Inspect condition of premises, and arrange for necessary maintenance or notify owners of maintenance needs.
Conduct seminars and training sessions for sales agents to improve sales techniques.
Rent or lease properties on behalf of clients.
Locate and appraise undeveloped areas for building sites, based on evaluations of area market conditions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Google Docs, HUD-1 software, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Argosy Legal Systems Power Closer, Front Desk, Showing Suite HomeFeedback, Showing Suite HomeFollowup.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software, RealtyStar AgentOffice.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: IBM Lotus 1-2-3, Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: Microsoft Project, Microsoft Teams, Telluride Software Classic Trak-It.
